s1.syndrome_frame: Episodic hypertension with micturition-related syncope and symptoms of catecholamine excess
salient_findings: Micturition-related episodes of headaches, diaphoresis, palpitations, chest pain, and presyncope
Tachycardia and significant blood pressure lability
Elevated plasma free metanephrine levels and isolated normetanephrine elevation in 24-hour urinary metanephrines
Bilateral crackles on pulmonary examination and pink, frothy secretions from endotracheal tube
key_facts: 2-year history of episodic hypertension
Micturition-related syncope
Episodic chest pain, palpitations, and diaphoresis
Tachycardia with a heart rate of 112 beats/min
Blood pressure of 196/120 mmHg
High-sensitivity troponin T of 936 ng/L, peaked at 1026 ng/L
N-terminal pro-BNP of 49 pg/mL
Plasma free metanephrine levels with isolated elevation in plasma normetanephrine (36 nmol/L)
24-hour urinary metanephrines with isolated normetanephrine elevation (8990 mcg)
Free norepinephrine of 21,685 pg/mL
Mildly depressed left ventricular systolic function (EF 40-45%) with hypokinesis of septum and inferolateral wall
Bilateral hilar opacities suggesting acute pulmonary edema on chest radiography
1.9 cm × 2.8 cm contrast-enhancing mass in bladder wall with surrounding lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen
